title: Grateful Dead Live at Mammoth Gardens on 1970-04-24
lineage: AUD > master C-120 > reel 3.75ips > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN > WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough, tinny audience recording that’s been cleaned up enough to showcase a stellar Dark Star and an electrifying Eleven.
ai_review.review: The tape is an early‑1970 AUD with limited fidelity – listeners report tinny mids, bottomless lows and occasional pitch quirks, though Sir Mick’s cleanup makes it tolerable. Musically the show shines, especially the second set where a classic Dark Star flows into a soaring St. Stephen and one of the era’s finest renditions of The Eleven, with Easy Wind and Friend of the Devil also highlighted.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the performance (especially Dark Star, The Eleven, Easy Wind) despite consistent complaints about the low‑fidelity audience source; weighted average yields a strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tinny, bottomless sound with limited frequency range; occasional pitch fluctuations. Sir Mick’s remaster reduces some issues but the recording remains rough and requires patience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows tightly with Dark Star into St. Stephen and The Eleven; acoustic set is weaker but still captures the band’s early‑1970 vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar cuts through clearly; reviewers note he “goes OFF” on Dark Star and delivers an intense Eleven.
band_member_comments.Phil: Hard to hear Phil’s bass in the acoustic portion, but no major complaints about his playing elsewhere.
